# soulsensis

> Your soul knows best. Listen to your soul. All it has wanted is to be heard. Honest essays from one person still working it out, for anyone who feels stuck, rushed or half alive. Written by a human. Published anonymously as soulsensis. The book: Sit Still Enough to Hear It (Essays on the tiredness of performing a life, and the way home to contentment).

## The book

- [Sit Still Enough to Hear It](https://soulsensis.com/book.html): essays on comparison, wanting, the shadow, blame, attention, surrender and contentment. Not self-help steps; one person thinking honestly from inside their own life.
- The book is being finished as one larger book, with the author's journals added, so the page count and contents may change.

## Topics (the book's chapters)

- [Chapter 1: A fraction of who I am](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-1): Comparison, living by someone else's script, and the wanting and waiting that keep you small.
- [Chapter 2: Behind lucid eyes](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-2): Facing what hurts instead of hiding it: dark thoughts, the shadow, friendships that end, and seasons that pass.
- [Chapter 3: Water the grass in front of you](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-3): Dropping blame, framing events as neutral, choosing where attention goes, and seeing that identity can change fast.
- [Chapter 4: The cost of fighting yourself](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-4): The addiction to stress and resistance, and why becoming yourself is the simplest and the most demanding thing.
- [Chapter 5: Sit still enough to hear it](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-5): No longer trying to shine, stepping aside from wanting, and coming home to the quiet voice underneath.
- [Chapter 6: Contentment, the only destination](https://soulsensis.com/essays.html#chapter-6): Living it: presence, meaning found by acting in the world, and a soul that was never broken.

## Questions

- [Why do I feel like I'm just existing?](https://soulsensis.com/question/just-existing-not-living/): You're living a life you can't authentically call your own. You struggle to look at yourself in the mirror.
- [Why do I always feel rushed?](https://soulsensis.com/question/why-do-i-always-feel-rushed/): Acceleration only gets you to a place faster. It does not mean you are happier. It just means you will have another goal sooner.
- [How do I find my purpose in life?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-find-my-purpose/): The thing that you come here to do is actually not linked to what you think makes you money.
- [How do I listen to my intuition?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-listen-to-my-intuition/): So, listen, deeply, your soul's nudges. Those quiet intuitive callings are 10x more powerful than what the mind can conceive.
- [How do I stop a habit I know is hurting me?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-stop-a-habit-hurting-me/): So the only way you can truly get rid of any vice that you know is not good for you is if you simply just stop resisting.
- [How do I stop waiting for the right moment?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-stop-waiting-for-the-right-moment/): The conditions are never right. The moment is the only moment. And the person who has to arrive is the one already standing here.
- [How do I stop needing other people's approval?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-stop-needing-approval/): The acceptance and pride I wanted from others were the acceptance and pride I had not yet given myself.
- [How do I let go of pain I keep holding on to?](https://soulsensis.com/question/how-do-i-let-go-of-old-pain/): If it has already given you what it had to give, you are allowed to put it down.
- [Why do I feel stuck in life?](https://soulsensis.com/question/why-do-i-feel-stuck-in-life/): This wanting is what traps you, and forcing change doesn't work. The more you grip to wanting, the further the object of your wanting moves away from you.
- [Why do I wake up with a feeling of dread?](https://soulsensis.com/question/why-do-i-wake-up-with-dread/): This desperate wanting is precisely what is trapping me, as it places excess importance on not being in this depressive state.
